column1: # The SMT session's first half (aws/lab.sh LAB_SUITE=transport LAB_PAIR=a
# LAB_SETS_FILE=<this file>; the matrix's arms are kept): SMT off, as every
# other session (vm.sh transport-tune), on c7i.4xlarge (Intel, 8 cores x 2
# threads; with SMT off 8 CPUs, one a core). transport-aws-smt.tsv is the
# other half, SMT on, on its own pair of the same type. TCP only: ergon-io's
# UDP has no uring backend.
#   mio-tcp              mio, epoll with SO_BUSY_POLL 50 us: the baseline
#   eio-tcp              ergon-io epoll-spin, busy_poll_us 50
#   eio-tcp-sqpoll-core  ergon-io uring-sqpoll, its SQPOLL thread on the next
#                        isolated core ({next_core}), no SO_BUSY_POLL
#   aa                   mio-tcp again
# Both halves run with the IRQ core capped at C1 (TR_IRQ_IDLE=auto: C1 under
# intel_idle, c7i's driver; every arm, read back per point and recorded in
# transport-settings.tr.env); `irq_idle 1` stops a session whose hosts would
# give anything else before its first point. The first SMT sessions ran uncapped, and the
# c7i diagnosis (transport-aws-c7i-diag.tsv) showed the IRQ core's wake from
# C6 dominating their 10k msg/s points: rerun both halves, never one.
# One stream, ping/pong round trips at 10k, 50k and 200k msg/s, LAB_REPS=3:
# 36 points (LAB_ESTIMATE=1 gives the hours).
smt off
irq_idle 1
# set     pair par host loads              streams netem arms
set smtoff a   -   ab   10000,50000,200000 1       -     mio-tcp,eio-tcp,eio-tcp-sqpoll-core,aa
